title: Required notation of the Schedule II opioid partial-fill right
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 22(c) any prescription issued by a practitioner for an OPIOID substance contained in Schedule II SHALL INCLUDE A NOTATION on the prescription that the patient may fill it, upon request, in compliance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 18(d3/4) in an amount NOT TO EXCEED THE FULL PRESCRIBED QUANTITY. The notation is a prescription-content duty on the prescriber that accompanies the patient's statutory right to receive a lesser quantity on request.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate recognises that Massachusetts both compels the partial fill on patient request and requires the Schedule II opioid prescription itself to disclose that right.

authority.name: Contents of prescription written by practitioner

exceptions: The notation duty reaches prescriptions for opioid substances in Schedule II; it is not a general notation requirement for every controlled-substance prescription.
common_confusions: Treating the notation as a pharmacy recordkeeping step rather than a prescriber prescription-content duty.
Assuming the absence of the notation removes the patient's s. 18(d3/4) right to request a lesser quantity.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 22(c) read verbatim on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-02 during Study Guide REPAIR-V3, remediating the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V2 finding that the s. 22(c) notation had no canonical representation. Independent audit still required.
